source.title: Better Training using Weight-Constrained Stochastic Dynamics
source.authors: B. Leimkuhler; Tiffany J. Vlaar; Timothée Pouchon; A. Storkey

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training outcomes on several classification tasks, including CIFAR-10, but does not test whether gradient-based training from random initialization reaches near-zero training classification error under the claim versions' conditions. Its CIFAR-10 results compare constrained and unconstrained optimization mainly on test performance.
record.gate_note: Training-error evidence is limited to a Fashion-MNIST statement that both methods quickly reached 100% training accuracy. Other training-loss plots and discussion do not report numeric classification error or results aimed at the claim versions. Cited statements about other studies are not this paper's results.
record.test_reason: Figure 4 compares standard and orthogonal initialization under otherwise matched SGD training across depths of plain ReLU MLPs on spiral data. Its accuracy trajectories bear on V4's initialization-dependent learning speed in a new setting. However, the supplied text does not preserve the plotted curves or state which initialization learns faster.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion that circle and orthogonality constraints improve classification generalization relative to the tested unconstrained and soft-constraint approaches. This should not imply universal superiority: Table D3 reports lower transformer validation losses for carefully tuned SGD with weight decay than for the circle-constrained method.
record.recipe_differences: The paper introduces constrained stochastic dynamics and compares them with SGD and soft constraints; it does not reproduce the claim versions' training-error studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports outcomes varying constraint type, optimizer, network depth, temperature, stepsize, penalty strength, and dataset, but these do not test the claim versions' training-error outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Maintaining orthogonality throughout training outperforms standard initialization, orthogonal initialization alone, and soft orthogonality penalties on spiral test accuracy for deeper MLPs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preserving weight orthogonality during training can improve generalization relative to initialization alone or soft penalties.

fits_no_version.finding: Both optimizers quickly reach 100% training accuracy in a 1000-node single-hidden-layer perceptron trained on 10,000 Fashion-MNIST examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wide fully connected ReLU networks can interpolate this reduced Fashion-MNIST training set.

fits_no_version.finding: Orthogonal initialization worsens ResNet-34 generalization on CIFAR-10 according to Appendix D.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Orthogonal initialization can worsen generalization in batch-normalized residual CNNs.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 139, 2021
record.problems: The paper's classification experiments emphasize test performance and generalization. It gives no numerical training classification error on CIFAR-10 and does not report CIFAR-100 results. The sole explicit training-accuracy statement concerns Fashion-MNIST and does not evaluate the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the reported classification outcomes do not test the specified training-error claims. The Fashion-MNIST statement that both methods reached 100% training accuracy is outside the versions' stated benchmark and conditions.

untested.parts: Training classification error of convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels and model-size or regularization conditions. CIFAR-10 training cross-entropy does not directly establish training classification error.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized CNNs and matched identity-shortcut controls; special deep tanh initialization and Fixup.

Activation matching and signal/gradient preservation as mechanisms; orthogonal versus equal-variance Gaussian initialization in deep tanh networks; orthogonal convolution kernels and extreme trainable depth. Figure 4 only compares initialization through test-accuracy trajectories in 2–12-hidden-layer ReLU MLPs.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability threshold, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence relative to measured thresholds.
Matched comparisons with and without batch normalization, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training speed or stability.

missing.what: Separate standard-initialization and orthogonal-initialization SGD accuracy trajectories for each tested depth. Both use h = 0.1, 5% subsampling, and averages over 10 runs. These comparisons are omitted and not declared in rows_left_out. Recover the plotted curves before assigning a directional V4 verdict.
missing.locator: Section 5.1, Figure 4, first and second columns; Appendix D.1

record.verdict_notes: The record overlooks the initialization control in Figure 4. No directional V4 label is justified from the supplied text because the relevant curves are unreadable and their relative learning speeds are not stated. Comparisons of constraints maintained throughout training do not isolate initialization effects.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sufficiently large convolutional networks reach zero or near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; effects of model size, early stopping and regularized recipes.
Whether extra student width reduces spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Whether plain batch-normalized networks degrade in training error with depth, whether identity shortcuts prevent this, or whether specified special initializations or Fixup allow deep training.
Whether activation-matched or orthogonal initialization changes training speed or trainable depth, including 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks.
Whether training recovers above an initial stability limit or whether sharpness tracks a stability threshold.
Whether batch normalization speeds accuracy gains or permits higher learning rates, or whether Fixup trains residual networks without normalization at comparable speed and stability.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
